title: How do we build a rectangle from one side and a diagonal?
description: A rectangle with a side of five centimetres and a diagonal of seven centimetres is built with a ruler, a set square and a compass. Keeko's doubt is about where the compass point goes, and the video breaks it.
teaching_notes: One idea: the compass arc is drawn from the end of the diagonal that is on the base, with the opening equal to the diagonal. Watch for students who put the compass point at the corner where the perpendicular line starts.

source: Construct a rectangle where one of its sides is 5 cm and the
video_script.why: A learner builds a rectangle from one known side and the diagonal, drawing the base first and then using a compass arc of the diagonal's length.
video_script.substitution: the book's rectangle ABCD with the base DC of five centimetres and the diagonal DB of seven centimetres
video_script.anchor: the book's rectangle ABCD with the base DC, the line el at C and the diagonal DB
video_script.wrong_answer: put the compass point on cee to draw the arc
video_script.wrong_move: puts the compass point at the corner where the perpendicular starts, so the arc measures a side and not the diagonal
video_script.payoff_line: The rectangle has sides of five centimetres and about four point nine centimetres. Its diagonal is seven centimetres.

final_answer.value: rectangle ABCD with DC = AB = 5 cm, AD = BC about 4.9 cm and diagonal DB = 7 cm
final_answer.spoken: a rectangle with sides five centimetres and about four point nine centimetres, and a diagonal of seven centimetres

maths_rules: the base DC is 5 cm and the line l at C is perpendicular to DC
B lies on l and is 7 cm from D, because the diagonal DB is 7 cm
the other sides AD and BC are equal, about 4.9 cm, since 7 x 7 - 5 x 5 = 24 and the square root of 24 is about 4.9
opposite sides are equal and all angles are 90 degrees
video_script.design: The rectangle ABCD is built on the board in four steps. The compass opening of seven centimetres stays visible while the arc is drawn from D.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about building a rectangle.
<bookmark mark='sizes'/>One side is five centimetres, and one diagonal is seven centimetres.
How will you start the drawing?

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.open: a compass is opened to a set length
marks.arc: the compass draws a curved piece of a circle, labelled arc

narration: <bookmark mark='open'/>A compass keeps the same opening that we set on it.
<bookmark mark='arc'/>A curved piece of a circle drawn with it is called an arc.

beats.on_screen: Given: a rectangle with a side of 5 cm and a diagonal of 7 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a rectangle with one side of five centimetres and one diagonal of seven centimetres.

marks.find: the task is written under the given line

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to construct this rectangle with a ruler and a compass.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: draw the base DC = 5 cm; at C draw a line l perpendicular to DC (90 degrees)

marks.base: the base DC of 5 cm is drawn
marks.line: a line l is drawn upwards at C, perpendicular to DC

narration: <bookmark mark='base'/>Step one, draw the base dee cee of five centimetres.
<bookmark mark='line'/>At cee, draw a line el perpendicular to dee cee.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: open the compass to 7 cm, put the point on D and draw an arc that cuts l; the cutting point is B (DB = 7 cm)

marks.arc: the compass with its point on D draws an arc of 7 cm that cuts the line l
marks.bee: the point B is marked where the arc cuts l

narration: <bookmark mark='arc'/>Step two, open the compass to seven centimetres. Put its point on dee and draw an arc across el.
<bookmark mark='bee'/>Call the cutting point bee, so that dee bee is seven centimetres long.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: draw a perpendicular to DC at D and a perpendicular to BC at B; they meet at A

marks.perps: a perpendicular to DC is drawn at D and a perpendicular to BC is drawn at B
marks.eigh: the point A is marked where they meet

narration: <bookmark mark='perps'/>Step three, draw a perpendicular to dee cee at dee. Draw another to bee cee at bee.
<bookmark mark='eigh'/>They meet at a point that we call eigh.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: check: AB = 5 cm, AD = BC, all angles 90 degrees, diagonal DB = 7 cm

marks.check: the sides and the diagonal are measured with a ruler and the four right angles are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='check'/>Step four, check the figure. Eigh bee is five centimetres, and the diagonal is seven centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Answer: rectangle ABCD with DC = AB = 5 cm, AD = BC about 4.9 cm, diagonal DB = 7 cm

marks.res: the other two sides are measured about 4.9 cm

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The rectangle has sides of five centimetres and about four point nine centimetres. Its diagonal is seven centimetres.
<bookmark mark='res'/>All four angles of the rectangle are ninety degrees.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the finished rectangle
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

marks.doubt: Keeko's bubble appears beside the corner C
marks.fix: an arc from C is drawn and it cuts l seven centimetres from C, marked as a side
marks.keep: the bubble is struck out and the arc from D is shown again

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks we should put the compass point on cee to draw the arc.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But then the arc would cut el seven centimetres from cee. That would make a side seven centimetres long.
<bookmark mark='keep'/>The diagonal joins dee to bee, so the point goes on dee.
